description: Single configuration record describing how an external frontend integrates with this Frappe backend over HTTP. This DocType documents and surfaces the integration; the real linking uses native Frappe tools (User API Access, OAuth Client, Webhook).

fields.description: Master switch indicating that an external frontend is integrated with this backend. This is a documentation/coordination flag; it does not start or stop the API.
fields.label: Integration Enabled

fields.description: Public base URL of the external frontend that consumes this backend, for example https://salis-fleet.com.
fields.label: Frontend Base URL

fields.description: Version of the documented API contract the frontend is built against. Additive changes are safe; breaking changes increment this value and require a notice to integrators.
fields.label: API Contract Version

fields.description: CORS origin(s) an administrator should add to allow_cors in site_config.json so the frontend can call this backend, for example https://salis-fleet.com. This field only records the intended origins; it does not modify server configuration.
fields.label: Allowed Origins

fields.default:
Integrating an external frontend

This app is the backend and source of truth. An external frontend (any stack: React, Vue, Flutter, native mobile, etc.) consumes it over HTTP. The paths below are the whole of it; nothing further is kept in this repository.

The stack does not decide how you authenticate — where the credential can live does. The real linking uses native Frappe tools; do not reimplement them here:

  • Confidential client (your own server, container, scheduled job, or a backend-for-frontend you operate) — use token auth: open a User record, generate an API Key + API Secret under API Access, and send the header Authorization: token <api_key>:<api_secret>. Token auth is stateless and CSRF-exempt, so it works reliably from an external origin.
  • Public client (a page running in the user's browser, or an app installed from a store) — never ship it an API secret. Whatever that client can read, its user can read out of the bundle, the network log, or device storage, and the secret authenticates as its user everywhere that user can reach. Use the native OAuth Client DocType with grant type Authorization Code plus PKCE, so each login proves itself with a one-time verifier and nothing long-lived is stored on the device; or place a backend-for-frontend of your own in front, keep the key and secret there, and let the browser or app talk only to that service.
  • Webhook: use the native Webhook DocType to push outbound events to the frontend (or any service) when documents change.

Whichever path you take, the permission model does not move: the backend still enforces every rule per user. Remember to add the frontend origin to allow_cors in site_config.json.
fields.label: Integration Help

fields.description: Master switch for outbound WhatsApp/SMS messages (worker Masar links, ride and request status). When OFF (default), every send is a logged no-op. Turn ON only after the gateway URL and API key below are set.
fields.label: Enable Messaging Gateway

fields.description: Preferred channel passed to the gateway. The gateway provider decides actual delivery; this is the channel hint sent in the request payload.
fields.label: Default Channel

fields.description: HTTPS endpoint of the generic message-send gateway, for example https://gateway.example.com/v1/messages. The app POSTs a JSON body { to, message, channel, sender_id } to this URL with the API key as a Bearer token. Provider-agnostic; the operator points this at their own WhatsApp/SMS provider or middleware.
fields.label: Gateway URL

fields.description: Secret API key/token for the gateway, sent as an Authorization: Bearer header. Stored encrypted; never echoed back to the client.
fields.label: Gateway API Key

fields.description: Optional sender id / from number the gateway should send as (when the provider requires it). Sent as sender_id in the request body.
fields.label: Sender ID / From Number

fields.default:
Outbound WhatsApp / SMS

This app does not bundle a WhatsApp/SMS provider. It POSTs a small JSON message to a generic HTTP gateway you operate or subscribe to, so any provider (Twilio, an official WhatsApp Business API host, a local SMS aggregator, or your own middleware) can be wired without code changes.

Set the Gateway URL and API Key above, then turn on Enable Messaging Gateway. The app sends, per message:

POST <Gateway URL>
Authorization: Bearer <Gateway API Key>
Content-Type: application/json

{ "to": "+9665...", "message": "...", "channel": "WhatsApp", "sender_id": "..." }

Adapt your provider or a thin middleware to accept that shape (or place a small translator in front of the real provider). While the gateway is disabled or unconfigured every send is a safe, logged no-op — nothing is dispatched.
fields.label: Gateway Help
